findings.title: A zero-byte artifact raises an uncaught NoMethodError, breaking fail-closed verification at the CLI boundary
findings.recommendation: One line at verifier.rb:563: bytes = file.read(max_bytes + 1).to_s. This preserves the existing downstream comparisons and routes an empty document through JSON.parse, which already yields the correct typed InvalidArtifactError and CLI exit code 2 with no CLI change. Add the regression case beside the existing malformed-input coverage in test/evals_verifier_test.rb.
findings.note: File#read returns nil (not "") at EOF for a zero-length file opened File::RDONLY|File::NONBLOCK; confirmed on Ruby 3.3.11 (size 0 -> nil, size 1 -> 1 byte). Probe: verify(<0-byte file>) -> NoMethodError at verifier.rb:564; CLI.run(["verify", <0-byte file>]) -> uncaught NoMethodError with empty stdout and stderr and no exit code. Whitespace-only files correctly return exit 2. The other eight malformed-input probes (absent, truncated, unknown type, digest absent/null, non-JSON, duplicate key, directory) all fail closed with typed errors.

findings.title: A pass row is decided by exit status and a nonzero run count, so a zero-assertion case would be recorded pass
findings.recommendation: Add one clause to run_case's outcome chain treating summary[:assertions].to_i.zero? as not-run, exactly as skips is already treated at script/generate_requirements_audit:93-95. SUMMARY_LINE already captures the value.
findings.note: Mechanism proven with a synthetic zero-assertion case (1 runs, 0 assertions -> exit 0 -> pass). Measured across all 251 distinct evidence references backing the 499 pass rows using the generator's own filter: 0 vacuous cases, so the hole has no current occupant. Recorded as a contract gap, not a present falsehood.
